jev-route-questions.yaml:
# Stage questions for `omni-dev ai jev route` (#1779), as Jev `choice`
# questions. `route` adds one criterion per tier (name -> description) to
# each question; the `none` criterion below is the only fixed option.
#
# The wording is the text validated against jev-1.13.0. Every question ends
# with the same bar sentence, which replaced an earlier "pick the cheapest
# class" that pushed every answer down a tier. Rewording shifts answers across
# the board, so re-run the evaluation before changing a word.
stage_design:
  type: choice
  instructions: >-
    Which class should do the design work that remains before implementation can start: choosing
    the approach, settling open questions, and writing a plan? Choose the least capable class likely
    to complete this stage correctly with no rework, about 9 times in 10. Judge the work that
    remains given the text, not the size of the text.
  criteria:
    none: "No design work remains: the text already settles the approach and the open questions."
stage_implement:
  type: choice
  instructions: >-
    Assume any remaining design work has been completed well. Which class should write the code,
    tests and docs? Choose the least capable class likely to complete this stage correctly with no
    rework, about 9 times in 10. Judge the work that remains given the text, not the size of the
    text.
  criteria: {}
stage_review:
  type: choice
  instructions: >-
    Which class should review the finished change before merge, so that mistakes the automated
    tests would miss are caught? Choose the least capable class likely to complete this stage
    correctly with no rework, about 9 times in 10. Judge the work that remains given the text, not
    the size of the text.
  criteria: {}
jev-route-tiers-anthropic.yaml:
# Effort capabilities checked 2026-10-01; criteria are uncalibrated routing hypotheses.
# The `anthropic` model ladder for `omni-dev ai jev route` (#1779, #1820):
# sonnet (Claude Sonnet) / opus (Claude Opus).
#
# A rung names a model family and its description a capability level, not a
# version: Jev reads only the description, and mapping a rung to a current
# model is the consumer's job. See docs/jev.md, "Rungs, model versions and
# effort".
#
# The `fable` rung is commented out, not deleted (#1903): Anthropic's own
# comparison reports Claude Opus 5.5 (released 2026-09-22) performing "at the
# level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work" and beating it on published coding
# benchmarks, so a distinct, more-capable-than-`opus` class is no longer
# supported by the evidence. Restore it by uncommenting the block below if
# that changes. This is a routing-ladder change only: `claude-fable-5-1`
# remains registered in src/templates/models.yaml for other, unrelated uses.
#
# Tiers are listed from least to most capable; `route` ranks them by position.
# The descriptions were re-evaluated against jev-1.13.0 in #1885; they are
# not the original #1779 wording. Rewording them shifts answers. The
# other providers' ladders (`jev-route-tiers-<provider>.yaml`) still carry
# three rungs and reuse these descriptions rung for rung where they overlap —
# an edit to a rung kept here is an edit to every ladder's matching rung.
# `--tiers FILE` replaces the ladder (at least two tiers, unique names; `none`
# is reserved for the design stage).
tiers:
  - name: sonnet
    models:
      - name: claude-sonnet-5-5
        verified: "2026-10-01"
        sources: [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort]
        effort:
          kind: configurable
          control: output_config.effort
          supported_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
          levels:
            - name: low
              description: >-
                The stage is short, local and familiar, with explicit requirements and an obvious solution or review checklist.
            - name: medium
              description: >-
                The stage needs several reasoning steps and checking ordinary interactions, with a clear approach and bounded scope.
            - name: high
              description: >-
                The stage needs sustained reasoning about subtle behavior, multiple components, non-obvious failure modes or competing approaches.
            - name: xhigh
              description: >-
                The stage needs extended exploration, long-horizon implementation or review, or repeated testing of interacting hypotheses beyond high effort.
            - name: max
              description: >-
                The stage approaches this model's capability limit and requires its deepest supported analysis; lower effort would leave major unresolved risks.
    description: >-
      Reliable at implementing and reviewing well-scoped work across several files, including
      debugging and non-obvious interactions when the approach is clear. May need help with complex,
      open-ended design requiring sustained judgement.
  - name: opus
    models:
      - name: claude-opus-5-5
        verified: "2026-09-23"
        sources: [https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort]
        effort:
          kind: configurable
          control: output_config.effort
          supported_levels: [low, medium, high, xhigh, max]
          levels:
            - name: low
              description: >-
                The stage is short, local and familiar, with explicit requirements and an obvious solution or review checklist.
            - name: medium
              description: >-
                The stage needs several reasoning steps and checking ordinary interactions, with a clear approach and bounded scope.
            - name: high
              description: >-
                The stage needs sustained reasoning about subtle behavior, multiple components, non-obvious failure modes or competing approaches.
            - name: xhigh
              description: >-
                The stage needs extended exploration, long-horizon implementation or review, or repeated testing of interacting hypotheses beyond high effort.
            - name: max
              description: >-
                The stage approaches this model's capability limit and requires its deepest supported analysis; lower effort would leave major unresolved risks.
    description: >-
      Reliable at complex, open-ended design and research: weighing architectures and unfamiliar
      approaches, anticipating failure modes, and making security-critical judgements. Carries subtle
      multi-file implementation and review through with sustained judgement.
